messages:
maria_dev: Quick follow-up from the RFC — I prototyped a tiny controller that does: 1) shadow X% traffic, 2) run warmup probes against the mirrored path, 3) when latency and error probes are within thresholds, ramp traffic with a latency-weighted step. Want feedback on the probe set and swapback triggers.

aj_platform: SGTM. What probes are you running? p95, p99, and a small synthetic load?

maria_dev: yes p95 + p99 + error-rate. also a cold-start probe: send a 20-token chat request with a pinned prompt to see model startup cost.

sahil_arch: Two asks: (A) how do you score cross-tenant variance? some tenants are noisy and will skew the p99. (B) what happens if the mirrored variant has lower throughput under sustained load?

maria_dev: good q. plan is per-tenant baselines and z-score normalization for alerts. for throughput we measure in-flight capacity and have a backpressure tag that prevents ramping if effective concurrency > 0.8 of observed capacity.

lina_sre: for SLO safety I want an early soft-fallback: if p95 increases by >20% for 10s during a step, revert immediately for that tenant but continue for others. also propose a global kill-switch. :fire_extinguisher:

aj_platform: Agreement on per-tenant fallback. One operational note: we need traceability so the swapback decision logs include the feature flags and model sha. otherwise oncall will be chasing ghosts.

maria_dev: absolutely. controller will emit a structured decision line to Kinesis, e.g.:

```
{controller_version: "v0.2.1", tenant: "acme", step_from: 5, step_to: 10, p95_old: 120, p95_new: 160, trigger: "p95_increase_33pct"}
```

maria_dev: Question for runtime: is it better to implement the latency-weighted ramp as part of the router or as a separate sidecar controller that edits route weights?

sahil_arch: Sidecar controller preferred. Reason: decouples routing logic from hot path, easier canary sim and replay, and we can unit-test the ramp policy outside the router. downside: extra eventual consistency window.

lina_sre: If sidecar, we need to shorten that eventual consistency. Can we add a TTL-based optimistic lock on route weights and a probe that fails fast if delta not applied within 500ms?

aj_platform: 500ms is tight but doable for most control-plane ops. For vendors/clouds we should degrade gracefully — treat missing immediate apply as "pending" and sample a small hedge traffic to both paths until settled.

maria_dev: ok that matches my mental model: sidecar edits weights, router reads weights with a small read-through cache, router has a hedging policy while weights are pending. Hedging window defaults to 1s.

lina_sre: operational playbook items: 1) metric for "swapback count per hour" 2) alert if swapbacks > 3 in 15m for same tenant 3) a searchable timeline for each swapback with traces attached.

aj_platform: also add a "rollback-reason" tag if the swapback is manual vs automated — helps separate flaky model regressions from infra issues.

maria_dev: noted. final question: any objections to using the cold-start probe as a mandatory gate on the first ramp for a variant (i.e., fail the first promotion if cold-start p95 > threshold)?

sahil_arch: No objection. One extension: tie it to instance warmup state — only gate the ramp if the variant pool reported healthy count < N to avoid false positives.

maria_dev: sweet. I'll update the RFC appendix with: probe set, per-tenant z-score normalization, sidecar ramp controller, hedging window, structured decision logs, and playbook items.

deploy-bot: Deployment: canary-controller v0.2.1 rolled to staging at 2026-03-21T15:42:30Z :white_check_mark:

maria_dev: thanks team — i'll circulate the appendix and drop a short demo tomorrow. :rocket:
